message.content:
Below is a minimal recipe you can run locally (or paste into your favourite HTTP client) that will give you **only** the identifiers (`id` values) of all CNAME‑record objects for `sample.com`. ```bash curl -s \ --request GET \ --url "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/sample.com/dns_records?type=CNAME" \ --header "x-apikey: secret123" | jq '[ .data[]?.attributes.id ]' ``` ### What happens step‑by‑step | Step | Command/Action | Result | |------|-----------------|--------| | 1️⃣ Request | `GET https://…/domains/sample.com/dns_records?type=CNAME`
with header `x-apikey: secret123`. | Returns a JSON payload containing *all* DNS records of type *CNAME*. | | 2️⃣ Filter | Query parameter `type=CNAME` limits the result set to CNAME entries only. | | 3️⃣ Extract IDs | Using `jq`, pull out `.data[].attributes.id` – the unique identifier assigned by VirusTotal to each DNS record. | | 4️⃣ Output | A plain array of those IDs, e.g.: `[ "abcd1234efgh5678ijkl9012mnop3456", ...]`. | #### Notes * If you prefer not to install `jq`, replace the last part with simple shell parsing, though `jq` keeps things tidy. * No other metadata (e.g., TTL, value) is shown—just the raw IDs. * Replace `secret123` with your real API key before running.
